name: Gaming and Leisure Properties, Inc.

profile.description: Gaming and Leisure Properties is the first REIT to specialize in the acquisition, financing, and ownership of gaming-industry real estate, leasing properties to leading regional gaming operators under long-term, triple-net master leases. The portfolio spans 66+ properties across 20+ states with tenants including PENN Entertainment, Bally's, Boyd Gaming, Caesars, and tribal operators. Market cap approximately $12.5 billion.

innovation.label: DEVELOPING
innovation.analysis: Track Record (2/3): GLPI pioneered the gaming-REIT category in 2013 and continues to expand with a $2.6B development pipeline, $700M Lincoln acquisition, and $467M Cordish commitment that drove Q1 2026 record revenue of $420M (up 6.3% YoY) and raised AFFO guidance to $4.08-$4.12 per share [1][2]. The recent expansion into tribal gaming represents a genuinely new revenue category. AI Deployment (0/2): No material AI deployment in the REIT's own operations — the business model is real-estate ownership and capital allocation, not technology [3]. Market Share (2/2): GLPI is the category-defining gaming REIT alongside VICI Properties, with a uniquely diversified tenant mix including regional operators, tribal gaming, and entertainment venues; the appointment of Carlo Santarelli from Deutsche Bank equity research as SVP Corporate Strategy reinforces strategic ambition [4]. Pipeline (2/2): $2.6B committed development pipeline plus tribal gaming expansion provide specific, multi-year revenue visibility through 2027+, with Q1 2026 results validating execution [1][2]. R&D Intensity (0/1): R&D is not a meaningful concept for a triple-net lease REIT.

inspiration.label: DEVELOPING
inspiration.analysis: Mission Floor (2/4): GLPI articulates a purpose around providing capital and real-estate solutions to the gaming industry while delivering stable, growing distributions — clear about what it does and for whom, but interchangeable with other specialty REITs and lacking a deeper societal purpose [3]. Community Impact (1/2): ESG Steering Committee oversees sustainability initiatives including energy efficiency, recycling, and water conservation across properties; Sustainalytics assigns a low controversy rating, but no distinctive community investment programs with specific dollar amounts were identified [3]. Employee Retention (1/2): Management team averages 11.5 years tenure, with CEO Peter Carlino's 12.67-year leadership and Brandon Moore's promotion from COO to President reflecting strong internal advancement and organizational continuity [4]. Insider Buying (0/2): Carlino retains equity from the 2013 PENN spin but no material net insider buying has been reported in the last 12 months.

infrastructure.label: STRONG
infrastructure.analysis: GLPI's financial profile is strong for a triple-net gaming REIT. Q1 2026 delivered record revenue of $420M (up 6.3% YoY) and net income of $239.4M, with full-year AFFO guidance raised to $4.08-$4.12 per share reflecting 5-6% growth from 2025's $3.88 [1][2]. ROE of 20.03% exceeds the 15% target, and profit margin of 55.06% reflects the capital-light lease model. Forward P/E of 13.04 is well within the 20 target. D/E of 181% is moderate for an investment-grade REIT. AFFO-based payout ratio of approximately 76% ($3.12 annual dividend / $4.10 midpoint AFFO) provides adequate coverage with room for dividend growth. Dividend track record is excellent: 12 consecutive years of payments since the 2013 spin-off and 11 consecutive years of increases [5]. Liquidity easily clears the $1M floor at ~2M average daily volume x $43.18 = ~$86M daily dollar liquidity.

ai_resilience.label: LOW RISK
ai_resilience.analysis: AI Risk Protection (8/9): GLPI owns physical casino real estate leased on long-term triple-net contracts to regulated gaming operators — AI structurally cannot replace gaming venues, gaming licenses, or the physical-real-estate ownership model [1]. Rent obligations are contractual and senior to tenant operating performance, so even if AI eventually pressured online vs. land-based gaming mix, GLPI's lease income would remain protected for the duration of master lease terms (most 15+ years with renewal options). The triple-net structure further insulates GLPI from technology disruption at the operator level. Analysts have not flagged AI as a disruption risk for gaming REITs [5]. AI Opportunity (0/1): GLPI generates no AI-related revenue; the business model has no AI monetization angle.

infinite_game.summary: GLPI is a stable, well-run specialty REIT with exceptionally long-tenured leadership and consistent capital allocation, but the business model is fundamentally about distributing cash to shareholders rather than pursuing a Just Cause that transcends the financial structure. The company benefits from patient capital deployment and disciplined underwriting, but strategic decisions are evaluated through a returns-on-capital lens rather than a broader purpose framework.

just_cause.analysis: Just Cause (1/3): GLPI's purpose is providing real-estate capital to the gaming industry and returning consistent yields to shareholders — distinctive for pioneering the gaming-REIT category in 2013 but ultimately a financial structure rather than a transformative societal cause [3]. Strategic decisions are driven by risk-adjusted returns, not a vision of a better future.

trusting_teams.analysis: Trusting Teams (2/2): Management team averages 11.5 years tenure with CEO Carlino's 12.67-year leadership providing exceptional continuity [4]. Brandon Moore's promotion from COO to President and Carlo Santarelli's external hire from Deutsche Bank demonstrate both internal advancement and strategic talent acquisition. The lean 22-employee corporate team operates with high empowerment, managing 66+ properties across 20+ states through trusted tenant relationships and delegated property management.

worthy_rivals.analysis: Worthy Rivals (0/1): GLPI competes principally with VICI Properties for gaming real estate acquisitions, but management commentary focuses on GLPI's own portfolio quality and deal pipeline rather than learning publicly from VICI's strengths or framing competition as self-improvement [1][2].

existential_flexibility.analysis: Existential Flexibility (1/2): GLPI has evolved from its PENN-leaseback origins into a diversified portfolio spanning PENN, Bally's, Boyd, Caesars, Cordish, and tribal gaming tenants — incremental but real strategic diversification [1][2]. The tribal gaming expansion represents a genuinely new market segment. However, the core triple-net lease model has remained unchanged since 2013.

courage_to_lead.analysis: Courage to Lead (1/2): Carlino has demonstrated disciplined underwriting — walking away from competitive auctions when pricing didn't meet return thresholds, and investing in the nascent tribal gaming segment that requires patient capital and complex sovereign-nation relationship management [1][4]. The $2.6B development pipeline represents a meaningful forward commitment. However, these are incremental bets within GLPI's existing competency rather than transformative, costly long-term wagers.

investment_thesis: GLPI delivered record Q1 2026 revenue of $420M (up 6.3% YoY) and raised full-year AFFO guidance to $4.08-$4.12 per share, reflecting 5-6% growth from 2025's record $3.88, driven by the $700M Lincoln acquisition, $467M Cordish commitment, and a $2.6B development pipeline [1][2]. The 7.2% dividend yield is supported by 12 consecutive years of payments and 11 years of increases, with an AFFO payout ratio of ~76% providing adequate coverage and room for growth. The triple-net master lease structure with 15+ year terms and rent escalators delivers predictable, contractually senior cash flow that is structurally protected from tenant operating volatility. Tribal gaming expansion opens a differentiated growth channel vs. VICI Properties, and the forward P/E of 13.04 offers reasonable value for a low-volatility, investment-grade specialty REIT.
thesis_continued: The bear case centers on leverage and growth limitations. Debt-to-equity of 181% and net debt-to-EBITDA of 5.41x constrain financial flexibility, particularly as higher-for-longer rates pressure refinancing economics on the $7B+ debt stack [2][5]. Revenue growth of 6.3% YoY and 5yr CAGR of ~4.5% is modest for a stock trading at a 7.2% dividend yield, suggesting the market is pricing in limited growth above the distribution. Dividend growth 5yr CAGR of only ~2.5% significantly trails the 6% target and barely exceeds inflation. The Inspire Impact Score of -1 (MIXED) reflects gambling exposure that may exclude GLPI from values-based mandates. Secular shifts toward online sports betting and iGaming could, over a 10-20 year horizon, weigh on land-based casino visitation and affect tenant lease coverage at renewal.
key_catalysts: Raised 2026 AFFO guidance of $4.08-$4.12 per share (up 5-6%) supported by $2.6B development pipeline, Lincoln, and Cordish commitments delivering incremental rental income [1][2]
Tribal gaming expansion creating a differentiated growth channel as the only gaming REIT with meaningful tribal relationships [1]
7.2% dividend yield with 12-year payment streak and ~76% AFFO payout providing income floor with room for distribution growth [5]
key_risks: Debt-to-EBITDA of 5.41x and D/E of 181% constrain refinancing flexibility in a higher-rate environment and limit acquisition capacity without dilutive equity issuance [2][5]
Tenant concentration with PENN Entertainment and Bally's — any credit deterioration at major tenants would pressure cash flow despite master-lease cross-collateralization [1]
Secular online gambling growth (iGaming, sports betting) could reduce physical casino traffic over a 10-20 year horizon, affecting tenant lease coverage and renewal economics [5]
